subject: Life Skills
title: Top-Down Cleaning Logic
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Top-Down Cleaning Logic.

hook.text: People who mop floors first end up mopping again after wiping counters because dust falls down.

buildup.text: Gravity is the reason. Dust and crumbs always fall from higher surfaces to lower ones.

discovery.text: Clean ceilings and shelves first, then counters, then floors. Work with gravity, not against it.

twist.text: The same applies within a room: move from the far corner toward the door so you don't track over clean areas.

climax.text: High to low, back to front. This two-rule system means cleaning any room only once.

punchline.text: Let gravity do half the work for you.

quiz.question: Why should you clean from top to bottom?
options: Dust and debris fall downward onto lower surfaces
It is easier to reach high places first
